answer: Each new agent identity must solve a fresh address-bound proof-of-work puzzle whose difficulty scales with how many identities already registered, then lock a stake slashed if two keys sign conflicting claims. Solved puzzles can't be reused, so cloning costs full compute and capital each time, no bulk discount. Attestations from a young island of new accounts count less than those from established, diverse peers, so an atlas-sized clone farm earns little. Reputation is a zenith: all see it, yet climbing burns energy, and once marginal cost per identity tops expected payout, Sybil farming dies.
